anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

The caller passed resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1. The process cwd never changes.

## 1. Resolve inputs and ROOT

- **Home:** acme/widget#12, `headRefName=fix/retry`, `headRefOid=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- **PRE_REWORK_HEAD** = `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- **MEMBER_HEADS**, in order:
  - `{13, acme/widget#13, <retry-cap title>, fix/cap, bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb}`
  - `{14, acme/widget#14, <retry-cap title>, fix/retry-docs, cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc}`

Commands, run from the primary at /work/widget:

1. `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` returns `/work/widget/.git`, so **ROOT=/work/widget**.
2. `git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` returns empty, so this is not a submodule.

## 2. Resolve the worktree home

- The overrides file has no `## using-git-worktrees` keys, so the legacy contract applies.
- There is no native worktree tool and no wrapper in `AGENTS.md`, the repo root, `script/` or `bin/`.
- The default home applies: `NAME=fix-retry`, **WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry**.

## 3. Fetch, then check reachability and remote equality for every PR

These checks run before any write.

1. `git -C /work/widget fetch origin` succeeds.
2. For each PR, both checks pass:

| PR | Object exists | Remote branch matches |
|---|---|---|
| #12 | `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}` | `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry` = aaaa…aaaa |
| #13 | `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}` | `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap` = bbbb…bbbb |
| #14 | `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}` | `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs` = cccc…cccc |

3. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main` gives **BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd**.

**Where a #14 failure would stop.** If #14's object were missing after the fetch, or `origin/fix/retry-docs` differed from `cccc…`, I would stop here with:

`PR #14 head ccccccc is not reachable (origin/fix/retry-docs is at <sha7>); the branch moved.`

That stop comes before the stop table, before `git worktree add` or checkout, and before any file or worktree write or merge.

## 4. Ordered stops (all pass)

1. `isCrossRepository` is false for all three PRs.
2. `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` shows no other path holding `fix/retry`.
3. Reachability passed in section 3.
4. The N=1 local-branch ancestry row does not apply (N=3), and no local `fix/retry` exists.

## 5. Recovery scan

There is no existing home worktree and no local home branch, so there is nothing to recover.

## 6. Provision the exact head (fresh creation)

1. Clean-base check: `git -C /work/widget status --porcelain` exits 0 with empty output, so the base is clean.
2. Home-safety check: `git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees` succeeds, so `.worktrees/` is already ignored and no `.gitignore` commit is needed.
3. Provenance check: `git -C /work/widget symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` gives an empty result, so the default branch is unresolved and I skip the note silently.
4. Checkout (row "No worktree, no local branch", unique-remote DWIM): `git -C /work/widget worktree add "/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry" fix/retry`. This is equivalent to `--track -b fix/retry … origin/fix/retry`.
5. Verify: `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns `aaaaaaa…`, which equals the home `headRefOid`.

## 7. Merge member heads, in listed order, using original heads

1. **#13:** save last-good = `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`, then run
   `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12" bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`
   The merge is clean and produces `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee`.
2. **#14:** save last-good = eeeeeee (full SHA via `rev-parse HEAD`), then run
   `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`
   The merge is clean and produces `Member merge: #14 fffffff`.

No conflict helper and no scoped runner are needed.

## 8. Merge the fetched base

`git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` is clean and records `merge: 1111111`.

## 9. Prove every original head is in the final HEAD

Each command exits 0:

1. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa HEAD` (#12)
2. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD` (#13)
3. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc HEAD` (#14)

PRE_REWORK_HEAD stays an ancestor. There was no rebase, reset or amend.

## 10. Fetch unresolved review threads

I run the `gh api graphql --paginate` reviewThreads query once per PR, with `-F o=acme -F r=widget` and `-F n=12`, then `-F n=13`, then `-F n=14`. Each succeeds with no unresolved threads, so each records `Threads: none`.

## Step 4 report

```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Ready to implement retry-cap rework for #12 (absorbing #13, #14)
```

MEMBER_HEADS go to gather. Nothing was pushed or closed, and no spec or plan was written.

I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

This is a synthetic narration; no tools are invoked. Every command below runs with **cwd `/work/widget`**. The process cwd never changes.

### 1. Resolve the PR worktree contract

The admitted-PR path replaces generic Steps 0 and 1.

1. Run:
   ```bash
   git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
   ```
   Resolve `GIT_DIR=GIT_COMMON=/work/widget/.git`, hence `ROOT=/work/widget`.

2. Run:
   ```bash
   git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
   ```
   Empty output confirms no submodule.

From the supplied facts, resolve:

- Home: `acme/widget#12`, branch `fix/retry`, original head `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- Members, in order: #13 at `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, then #14 at `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`.
- Base branch: `main`.
- `NAME=fix-retry`.
- `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.

There are no overrides, native tools, or wrappers. All PRs are in-repository. Use the built-in existing-branch checkout, not generic new-branch creation.

### 2. Fetch and validate before writes

Run, in order:

```bash
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs
```

Fetch succeeds. Each object exists; each remote resolves to its supplied full head SHA.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main
```

Resolve `BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget for-each-ref '--format=%(refname) %(objectname)' refs/heads/fix/retry
```

The listing contains only the primary checkout, with none of the admitted branches checked out. The local-home-branch query is empty. No recovery or local-branch ancestry check applies.

**Failure boundary:** An unreachable original #14 head or a mismatching `origin/fix/retry-docs` stops during these pre-write validations, before checkout, ignore-file changes, or any merge:

```text
PR #14 head ccccccc is not reachable (origin/fix/retry-docs is at <observed sha7>); the branch moved.
```

That failure does not occur in this case.

### 3. Check hygiene and provision

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
```

Status succeeds with empty output. The ignore check succeeds, so no `.gitignore` write or commit is needed.

Setting up an isolated worktree at `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` on branch `fix/retry` for this work.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

Unique-remote DWIM creates the tracking branch. The listing confirms the exact selected home. HEAD equals `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.

No setup installs or general test suites run.

### 4. Merge members, then fetched base

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m 'merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12' bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse --short HEAD
```

Save the original home SHA as the last-good head. The clean merge produces `eeeeeee`.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m 'merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12' cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse --short HEAD
```

Save the full SHA of commit `eeeeeee` as the next last-good head. The clean merge produces `fffffff`.

Run:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse --short HEAD
```

The clean base merge produces `1111111`. No conflict helpers or scoped tests are needed.

Prove preservation of every original head:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc HEAD
```

All three exit 0.

### 5. Step 4 report

```text
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Ready to implement retry caps
```

No generic provenance note applies to this PR-head report.

### 6. Fetch unresolved threads before gather

Run this exact shell command, still with cwd `/work/widget`:

```bash
for N in 12 13 14; do
  gh api graphql --paginate -f query='query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!,$endCursor:String){repository(owner:$o,name:$r){pullRequest(number:$n){reviewThreads(first:100,after:$endCursor){pageInfo{hasNextPage endCursor} nodes{id isResolved isOutdated path line originalLine comments(first:100){pageInfo{hasNextPage endCursor} totalCount nodes{url body author{login} createdAt}}}}}}}' -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n="$N"
done
```

The three invocations use final arguments `n=12`, `n=13`, and `n=14`, respectively. Each succeeds with empty output: record `Threads: none` for each PR. No comment-pagination calls are needed.

Stop here: no gather, spec, plan, push, or close operations.
